newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close down, further weakness seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close down, further weakness seen.

text.p: Singapore shares closed lower on Friday as the market corrected to reflect an overnight fall on Wall Street and continued disappointment in the annual results reported by domestic blue chips, dealers said.
The barometer Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended down 18.87 at 2,135.46 marking a new low for the year.

"We said the market would be weak through the early part of March, find a new low and then go up as it got the results it was expecting, but I don't think we've quite found the low point yet," said a dealer with a local brokerage.

Trade data due next week was not expected to guarantee lift. "After the first quarter export figures we'll know for sure whether the economy will go up towards the seven percent level or head down towards five percent," another dealer said.

The uncertainty depressed stocks. Losers overwhelmed gainers 304 to 91 on volume of 209 million shares. Singapore Press foreign stock lost a dollar to Singapore $26.60 and Singapore Airlines foreign hit a year low of S$11.90, down S$0.40.

Good news came for OUB Bank, whose shares were suspended ahead of news that 1996 net profits rose 19.7 percent to S$310.4 million, and debut stock Noble Group, which closed at US$0.975 up from its US$0.88 offer price. -- Nick Edwards (65 8703011)
